Values are never shown. It closes retest gaps G13 and G14; Rebuild from zero steps 10.1 to 10.5 point here. Its own tab next to GoHighLevel, so each tab has one writer. Facts from play spp-p20c (notes/gap-facts-apps.md §3 and §4). Built by work/2026-10-01_setup-playbook/build_tabs.py from tabs/ghl-rebuild.json; never edit this tab by hand.
Gateway 1. The HighLevel Marketplace app (fresh account)

Sign up at marketplace.gohighlevel.com (Sign Up, verify phone and email). The first person to sign up is the account's only Owner, so add teammates as users instead of sharing the login. An agency admin who clicks Sell on Marketplace gets one made from the agency's details.
Ours exists; it owns the app below.
1.2 Marketplace CLI (how our app is kept)

npm install -g @gohighlevel/marketplace-cli (needs Node 20.12 or newer), then ghl login (browser sign-in). Flow: ghl app create (or ghl app pull <app id>), ghl app validate, ghl app diff, ghl app push, ghl app publish.

@gohighlevel/marketplace-cli 1.0.0 at ~/.local/bin/ghl. The app's workspace ~/Development/increase-roas-marketplace-app is the private repo increaseroasir/increase-roas-marketplace-app (manifest, webhooks, .ghl CLI baselines; client secrets stay in the ghl CLI's secret ledger, never in the repo): a newcomer clones it, then runs ghl app pull <appId> to refresh.

My Apps > Create App: name, App Type Private (internal, not listed, installed with the app's own install link), listing type. Target user can't be changed once set. HighLevel's recommended setup for agency installs is Target user Sub-account with agency bulk install; an app that needs agency-level scopes (companies, oauth, saas, snapshots, custom menu links) must be installable by Agency Only.
Private; user types Company and Location (the legacy 'Agency & Sub-account' setting); white-label friendly; agency bulk install on; free; live version 5.0.0.

Advanced Settings > Auth > Select Scope (or ghl app scopes add): select the 175 scopes the gateway asks for, including oauth.readonly (list the installed sub-accounts) and oauth.write (mint sub-account tokens). Changing scopes later makes a new major version that each installer must accept.
175 allowed scopes, exactly the gateway's list (0 differences either way).

Add https://<your gateway Worker address>/oauth/callback (Advanced Settings > Auth). It must match what the Worker sends, which it builds from its own address. White-label apps can't use HighLevel-branded redirect URLs.
The gateway callback (the default), plus Composio's auth-app URL for a second client key used by the Hermes route (G24).
1.6 Client keys: where the credentials go

Advanced Settings > Auth > Client Keys > Add. HighLevel shows the Client ID and the Client Secret; the secret is shown only once. Save both straight into a new 1Password item, then pipe them into the Worker secrets GHL_CLIENT_ID and GHL_CLIENT_SECRET (section 2). Never paste them into chat or a file.
2 client keys: the default (the gateway's) and 'composio_hermes'. No 1Password item in Connectors holds the gateway's client ID or secret.

Advanced Settings > Webhooks: https://<worker>/webhooks/ghl and the events you want. The Worker posts each event to Slack when SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_CHANNEL_ID are set; events from another company are refused.
ghl app publish (or the portal). A private app goes live at once, with no review. A private app can be installed in up to 5 agencies.
1.9 Put your app and agency into the code
Set GHL_APP_ID in lib/gateway-core.mjs (line 2) to the new app's ID, and GHL_ALLOWED_COMPANY_ID in wrangler.toml to your agency's company ID. Tokens and webhooks for any other company are refused.
Leave HighLevel's 'UNUSED — not Agent Gateway' app alone; only the Agent Gateway app backs this Worker.
Recorded in the gateway's finish notes.
Gateway 2. The Worker increase-roas-oauth-gateway: settings and secrets
what it holds, and how to make it
increase-roas-oauth-gateway, worker.mjs, 2026-08-13. Keep your Worker's name in the SELF binding too.
wrangler d1 create <name>, put its ID in wrangler.toml, then create the tables in section 3: wrangler d1 execute <name> --remote --file <schema file with section 3's statements>.
The Worker calling itself; set service to your Worker's name.
Your agency's company ID. Everything for another company is refused.
The Slack channel for webhook events.
The app's client key (section 1, step 1.6), used to trade the sign-in code for tokens and to refresh them.
Exactly 32 random bytes, base64url-encoded. It encrypts the GHL tokens stored in D1. If it is lost, the stored tokens can't be read and the agency must sign in again at /oauth/start.
The gateway key: a random string of at least 16 characters. Composio sends it as Authorization: Bearer on /mcp. Save it in 1Password first (section 4, step 4.3).
Present; in 1Password as 'GHL OAuth CRM (ghl-oauth-crm) — gateway key'.
A second random key (at least 16 characters) for /api/* callers such as the HTL dashboard. /api/* also accepts the gateway key.

Present. Its value from the local .dev.vars is in 1Password item 'GHL OAuth CRM (ghl-oauth-crm) — INTERNAL_API_KEY (from local .dev.vars)' (2026-10-02); whether it equals the live Worker secret is NOT_PROVEN (Cloudflare never shows secret values).
A Slack bot token for posting webhook events.
Pipe each value from 1Password (or a script) into wrangler secret put <NAME>; that deploys a new version. Cloudflare never shows a secret's value again.

Gateway 3. D1 tables (exact statements read from the live database 2026-10-01)

CREATE TABLE agency_authorizations (company_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, user_id TEXT, scope TEXT NOT NULL, access_token_enc TEXT NOT NULL, refresh_token_enc TEXT NOT NULL, access_expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, installation_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE location_authorizations (company_id TEXT NOT NULL, location_id TEXT NOT NULL, user_id TEXT, scope TEXT NOT NULL, access_token_enc TEXT, refresh_token_enc TEXT, access_expires_at INTEGER, installation_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (company_id, location_id), FOREIGN KEY (company_id) REFERENCES agency_authorizations(company_id) ON DELETE CASCADE)
CREATE TABLE oauth_states (state_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, csrf_hash TEXT NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, used_at INTEGER)
CREATE INDEX idx_location_authorizations_company ON location_authorizations(company_id, location_id)
Gateway 4. Install at agency level, connect Composio, and keep it running

Signed in as the agency admin, open https://<worker>/oauth/start. HighLevel's consent page (chooselocation, user type Company) lists the scopes; choose the sub-accounts (bulk install). The Worker trades the code for agency tokens (user_type Company) and stores them encrypted.

Nothing to do by hand. On each call the Worker lists the app's installed sub-accounts (/oauth/installed-locations, needs oauth.readonly), mints that sub-account's token from the agency token (/oauth/location-token, needs oauth.write) and caches it.
A CRM read for one sub-account works (step 4.4).

Make a long random string (at least 16 characters) and save it first in the 1Password item 'GHL OAuth CRM (ghl-oauth-crm) — gateway key'. Pipe it from there into wrangler secret put GHL_MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY, then push the same item into Composio custom_ghl_oauth_crm with the key mover.

Through Composio custom_ghl_oauth_crm, a list-locations call returns the agency's sub-accounts. (This is the check G23 moved to step 10.2.)

Access tokens last about a day. A refresh token lasts up to a year or until it is used once, and each refresh returns a new pair. The Worker refreshes 120 seconds before expiry and stores the new pair.

Add the scopes to the app, publish the new major version, accept the update in the agency, then open /oauth/start again. When the agency's scope set changes, the Worker drops its cached sub-account tokens so new ones carry the new scopes.

A new Worker needs a new client key from the app (the secret can't be read back), a new TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY with a fresh agency sign-in at /oauth/start, and a new INTERNAL_API_KEY for /api callers. The gateway key can be restored from 1Password.
Builder 1. Deploy the builder origin on the hub (/opt/ghl-command-universal; after Phase 8)

The hub from Phase 8 already has Node 22 (/usr/bin/node), Python 3 (/usr/bin/python3) and Supervisor. The hub installer does not deploy the builder origin; these steps do. Clone github.com/increaseroasir/ghl-command-universal.

Make /opt/ghl-command-universal (mode 700). Copy origin/server.py, origin/test_origin.py, origin/package.json and origin/package-lock.json into it, then run npm ci there. That installs @elitedcs/ghl-mcp 3.88.2 from the public npm registry.
The copied files' sha256 equal git.
All four equal commit 6fcc3b4 by hash; 3.88.2 installed.
/opt/increase-roas-mcp/ghl-config must hold credentials.json, .ghl-tokens.json and device.json (table 2). The origin copies them into each new session and never edits the originals.
Present, 0600; the registry has 49 sub-account entries.

On the hub, write the key from 1Password item 5bfzdypjiimr7ov4kyua6wxtha ('GHL Command Builder (ghl-command-builder) — origin key') into /opt/ghl-command-universal/origin-key, mode 0600, with op inside a script (never typed or printed). The Worker's ORIGIN_KEY holds the same value. If the item is ever lost, make a new random key and set both places together.
Without the key, /health answers 401; the acceptance test (step 1.7) passes with it.
origin-key 0600; equal to the 1Password item by hash (spp-p20a).

Fresh account: create a remotely managed tunnel (API POST /accounts/<id>/cfd_tunnel with config_src cloudflare, or the dashboard). Set ingress <origin hostname> to http://127.0.0.1:8789 with a catch-all http_status:404, and add a proxied DNS CNAME to <tunnel id>.cfargotunnel.com. Rebuilding ours: fetch the token with GET …/cfd_tunnel/9b09467d-9c1c-4f4c-9b00-021ad8239f20/token through Composio custom_cloudflare_api into /opt/ghl-command-universal/tunnel/token (mode 0600). Put cloudflared 2026.9.3 at tunnel/cloudflared and check its sha256 against the README.
Cloudflare shows the tunnel healthy with 4 connections.
Healthy, 4 connections; ingress ghl-command-origin.increaseroas.com to 127.0.0.1:8789 plus the 404 fallback; proxied CNAME; cloudflared sha256 matches.

Copy origin/deploy/supervisor/ir-ghl-command-universal.conf and ir-ghl-command-tunnel.conf to /etc/supervisor/conf.d/, then supervisorctl reread and supervisorctl update (as the hub installer does for its own programs).
supervisorctl status shows both RUNNING, and 127.0.0.1:8789 is listening.
Both RUNNING; both files equal git by hash; python3 listening on 127.0.0.1:8789.

python3 /opt/ghl-command-universal/test_origin.py. It is read-only: auth, dispatcher gates, two-session isolation, live location identity, workflow listing, and hashes of the original config before and after.
Without the key, https://<origin hostname>/health answers 401 (the tunnel is up and the key is required).

how to get or make it

Buy at ghlcommand.com: $97 a month for every sub-account, on up to 3 machines (the hub counts as one). The key arrives by email.

Builder 3. The Worker ghl-command-universal: settings and secrets
what it holds, and how to make it
wrangler kv namespace create <name>, then put its ID in worker/wrangler.jsonc. Holds OAuth clients, one-use consent handles, grants and token state.
A random value. Change it to revoke every MCP token at once; apps then reconnect and approve with the current password.

64 lowercase hex characters: the SHA-256 of the connection password in 1Password item yxvess6diezoy7lgrnhqrmct5i ('GHL Command Builder (ghl-command-builder) — connection password'). Compute it in a script from the item and pipe it into wrangler secret put; never type the password. Rotating the password blocks new approvals but doesn't revoke tokens, so change AUTH_EPOCH too.

Builder 4. Register a sub-account's Private Integration key with the builder

In GHL, switch into the sub-account (not the agency view): Settings > Integrations > Private Integrations > Create Private Integration. Enable all scopes and copy the key at once; it is shown only once. Save it straight into 1Password as 'GHL PIT — <account>' with its location ID.
The 1Password item holds the key and the location ID.
4.2 Register it on the hub, not through Composio

The builder's public tools leave out register_location on purpose, so registration runs on the hub with GHL Command's own CLI against the original config: GHL_MCP_CONFIG_DIR=/opt/increase-roas-mcp/ghl-config /usr/bin/node /opt/ghl-command-universal/node_modules/@elitedcs/ghl-mcp/dist/index.js cli register-location --location-id <id> --api-key <key> --name "<account>". It checks the key with GHL live. Read the key from 1Password inside the same script; a key passed as an argument is briefly visible to other processes on the hub.
Exit code 0, and cli list-locations (which never prints keys) shows the account.

GHL Command's own note: seed while it is stopped, or restart it afterwards. Each builder session keeps the registry copy made when it started, so copy the new registry into every session folder (sessions/<id>/.ghl-tokens.json, mode 0600), then supervisorctl restart ir-ghl-command-universal.
Through Composio custom_ghl_command_builder: switch_location to the new location, then get_location returns the same ID. Switch back if the shared default changed.
